G L E U H R
Wellness Pvt Ltd
FRONT DESK MANAGER
Role · KRAs · KPIs · SOP · Consequences
Reports to: Saurabh (Operations Manager)  ·  Daily floor partner: Branch Manager  ·  Coordinates with: Senior Doctor
1  ·  Role Purpose
The Front Desk Manager owns the operational standard, audit discipline and client experience of the branch. Where the Branch Manager owns revenue and the branch as a whole, the FDM is the operations-and-experience specialist who makes sure every function inside the four walls runs to standard every day — and that what the client feels, from the moment they arrive to the moment they leave, is consistently warm, smooth and professional.
In one sentence.  Hold the branch to operational standard, keep every client's experience clean and complaint-free, and prove it with audit evidence.

The line is to operations, not to revenue.  The FDM does not report to the BM, and the BM does not report to the FDM. The BM owns branch revenue and the branch as a whole; the FDM owns operational standard, audit and client experience, and reports up the operations line to Saurabh. On the floor they are daily partners — the BM cannot hold the branch without a strong FDM, and the FDM cannot fix what only the BM can decide. Hold that partnership.
2  ·  Key Result Areas (KRAs)
Six KRAs. Each carries weight in monthly review.
KRA 1 — Operational Standard & Flow
Every function meets daily standard — reception, housekeeping, therapist cabins, waiting area
Patient wait time under 10 minutes; clients attended within 5 minutes of arrival
Smooth flow across reception, doctor, counsellor and therapist — no avoidable bottlenecks
No SOP bypassed by any function on any day
KRA 2 — Audit & Compliance
Daily audits across reception, housekeeping and therapist cabins
Compliance audit scores (Saurabh / Arshpreet) consistently at or above standard
3-strike corrective action on repeated violations
Cleanliness photos verified every round; findings logged
KRA 3 — Client Experience
NPS / CSAT above target
Complaint rate per 100 visits below threshold; DSAT closed the same day
Zero client complaint carried forward beyond the day it was raised
24-hour resolution SLA met on every logged complaint
KRA 4 — Operations Metrics & Reporting
Morning readiness report filed before clinic opens
End-of-day operations report filed on time
Weekly operations report to Saurabh on schedule
CRM / data accuracy at 100% for operational fields
KRA 5 — Team Standard (Operations)
Every operations report (reception, housekeeping) has a current scorecard
Underperformers on documented coaching plans, not protected
Therapist cabin standards held through regular audits (operational, not clinical)
Front-desk discipline — grooming, tone, phone usage — maintained
KRA 6 — Hygiene, Safety & Brand Stewardship
Cleanliness, AC, seating and refreshment standards held through the day
CCTV uptime verified daily; cash secured at closing with reception
Zero operational hard-line violations — off-system payments, data mishandling, unsafe shortcuts
Any reputational or safety risk escalated to Saurabh and founder the same day

4  ·  Standard Operating Procedure
Every working day follows this rhythm. The discipline is what makes the branch run, not heroics.
Morning  ·  Before clients arrive
Floor walk — reception, cabins, washrooms, refreshment area. Look at the branch as a client would.
Reception huddle (5 min) — yesterday's score, today's appointments, VIPs, risks.
Housekeeping huddle (5 min) — same-day standards, asks from yesterday.
Verify reception readiness — LED, AC, music, water station, washroom supplies.
Confirm the morning cleanliness photo is posted in the team group.
File the morning readiness report to Saurabh — staff availability, absentees, readiness.
The relationship with the BM-Doctor meeting
You feed the meeting; you do not run it.  The daily BM-Doctor meeting is run by the Branch Manager and the Senior Doctor as peers. The FDM's job is to make sure the operational truth reaches that meeting — accurate wait times, cabin audit findings, complaint patterns, and any operational issue blocking clinical work. Bring the evidence; let the peers decide. Then carry the operational actions back to the floor.
Through the day
Hourly floor rounds — waiting area, cabin readiness, hygiene, staff conduct.
Therapist cabin audit — signed checklist sample, hygiene, machine state, protocol adherence.
Live experience monitoring — watch for wait-time build-up and step in.
Complaint handling — resolve on the floor within SLA; log every case.
Asks register — anything raised by any team member, status updated.
Provide operational inputs to the daily BM-Doctor meeting — wait times, cabin issues, complaints.
Evening  ·  After clients leave
End-of-day operations report to Saurabh — readiness, audit findings, complaints, open issues.
Verify CCTV uptime and confirm cash secured with reception at closing.
Update the daily log — KPIs, sentiment, open issues.
Plan tomorrow — confirmed bookings, follow-ups, any concern carrying over.
5  ·  Monthly Rhythm  ·  Operations & Experience Review
Submitted monthly to Saurabh and reviewed in the operations review. Forward-looking, not a report on the past.
What it covers
Last month — audit scores, NPS, complaint trends; what worked, what didn't
This month's commitment — specific operational and experience targets
Top 3 issues to eradicate — with owner, due date, success criteria
Top 3 experience improvements — specific actions to lift NPS and reduce complaints
Team development — who is being coached on what (reception, housekeeping)
Asks of corporate — anything needed from Saurabh, BM, or central compliance
The plan, not the report.  Most monthly submissions are reports on the past. This is the opposite — five of its six sections look forward. The past month is one section out of six. That is by design.
6  ·  Authority and Escalation
What the FDM decides without escalation
Day-to-day operations scheduling and floor deployment
Reception / housekeeping scorecards and corrective coaching
Client complaint resolution within the 24h SLA
Operational readiness decisions on the floor
What needs Saurabh (Operations Manager) sign-off
Operations policy questions or SOP exceptions
Hiring or terminating an operations team member (with BM / RH)
Operational spend beyond branch limit
Any change affecting more than one function
What needs Compliance sign-off
Compliance findings that span branches (Arshpreet)
Hygiene / safety standards interpretation (Saurabh + Dr Kanikta)
What comes to Harman / Founder directly
Pressure to break a hard-line or safety rule
Serious client complaint with reputational risk
Regulatory or safety incident
Anything that feels structurally wrong
7  ·  Don'ts
Behaviours that are not acceptable, regardless of performance.
Overriding a clinical decision — clinical sits with the doctor, always
Hiding an operational problem or a complaint from Saurabh
Having favourites — a preferred function or person who gets softer audits
Allowing any operational hard-line violation — off-system payments, data mishandling, unsafe shortcuts
Carrying a DSAT case forward past the day it was raised
Skipping the morning or end-of-day report
Bypassing Saurabh to raise routine matters higher
Treating company decisions as suggestions
8  ·  Consequences Framework
Trigger
Response
Single-month miss on a KPI
Documented in 1-on-1 with Saurabh; cause analysis; corrective plan agreed
Two consecutive months miss on the same KPI
Written notice; 30-day improvement plan with weekly check-ins
Three consecutive months miss
Formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with HR + Saurabh
DSAT carried forward, repeatedly
Written warning
Morning / EOD report not filed, repeatedly
Written warning
Single operational hard-line violation (allowed or directed)
Same-day review; termination consideration
Serious dishonesty with Saurabh or founder
Single-incident termination consideration
9  ·  What 'Good' Looks Like — End of First Year
Branch operational audit scores consistently at or above standard.
NPS above target; complaints rare and always closed within SLA.
Reception and housekeeping hold the standard without daily firefighting.
Therapist cabins pass audit; hygiene and safety never in question.
Morning and EOD reports land on time, every day, with no chasing.
